correctness.rationale: Patey–Shafer Theorem 1.7 already proves for every finite k that BRT^3_{2,4} is not ≤^k_ω RT^2_2. A bounded-pair instance (l,f) is an ordinary RT^2_2 instance f; every infinite RT-homogeneous set must have color 0 because a color-1 infinite homogeneous set would violate the absence of an l-element color-1 homogeneous subset. Therefore each BRT pair oracle use simulates with exactly one RT pair use; a hypothetical finite-use bounded-pair reduction contradicts published Theorem 1.7. No experiments or extrapolation.
residual_risks: Finite-use only; says nothing about unrestricted omega-reducibility.
